basics.title: What this plugin is
paragraphs: Weave Incremental Reading turns “read later” into a sustainable queue: materials from Markdown, PDF, Canvas, web pages, and EPUB become schedulable reading points you can resume and jump back to.
It is a standalone incremental-reading controller. It can work with the Weave main plugin and Weave EPUB Reader, and also works on its own.

items: Reading point: one pending reading task with source tracing so you can jump back to the original location.
Topic (.irdeck): a container for reading points, stored as a topic file in your vault.
Incremental reading calendar: the main surface. Browse due, scheduled, and overdue points by date and keep a daily rhythm.
Unified “Add link” entry: paste web URLs, wikilinks, block refs, PDF++, Canvas nodes, or EPUB location links.
Material import and folder subscription: split Markdown or import PDF/EPUB chapters; optionally subscribe a folder so new notes are auto-added to a topic (premium).
Scheduling and resume: processing vs reading-list modes, daily caps and load smoothing; resume points jump back to source.
Continuous reading: expand related points from the same source document so you can advance through one note/book in order.
Associated notes: curated links for PDF / EPUB; outbound links from Markdown / web carriers (premium).
Source tracing: Markdown, PDF++, Canvas, web, and EPUB keep stable resume links.

basics.title: Using the calendar
paragraphs: Open the incremental reading calendar to see a month heatmap above and the selected day’s reading points below.

items: Top “+”: open Add reading target (the daily path).
Top “More” menu: import materials, update subscribed folders, data management, view modes, and more.
Pick a date to inspect that day’s queue; after reading, scheduling decides when it returns.
Right-click / long-press a reading point for scheduling, priority, continuous reading, associated notes, tag groups, and more.

basics.title: Continuous reading
paragraphs: Useful when one source document has been split into many reading points: advance through them by source instead of hunting for the next piece in the list.

items: Entry: reading-point context menu → More actions → Continuous reading.
When enabled, an expand control appears so you can show other reading points from the same source document.
This is part of basic scheduling assistance and does not require a premium license.

basics.title: Associated notes
paragraphs: Associated notes are split by reading-point type: PDF / EPUB use curated manual links; Markdown / web (excerpt-note carriers) use Obsidian outbound links for related-note stats and open actions.

items: Entry: reading-point context menu → Associated notes.
PDF / EPUB: open, append, create, set primary, remove, and other curated actions.
Markdown / web: open the source note and browse its outbound related notes; web points can also open the original URL in a browser.
Web reading points already create an excerpt Markdown carrier on add; only if that carrier is missing does the menu offer recreating it.
When curated links or outbound links exist, a Notes badge may appear on the list item.
Associated notes are premium: without activation the entry may be hidden, or shown locked if “Show advanced feature preview” is on.

basics.title: Tag groups
paragraphs: Tag groups let different materials use separate scheduling preferences and interval factors, with priority deciding which group wins when several match.
Note: tag groups are still being improved and may not work reliably yet. Do not depend on them as a daily workflow in the current release; later versions will continue to harden this path.

items: Settings: Settings → Weave Incremental Reading → Advanced scheduling → Tag group manager.
Calendar: reading-point context menu → Tag group (view or switch).
Tag groups are premium; until the feature is stable, prefer topics, priority, and basic scheduling to keep reading moving.

add.title: Recommended entry
paragraphs: For adding one reading point, use the Add reading target modal—not material import.
Import is for turning a whole document or book into many points. Add is for one link, one selection, or one Canvas node.

buttons.label: Add link
buttons.description: Primary control on the calendar toolbar

items: Paste a link, or use “Current location” to capture a Markdown block / line anchor.
Confirm the reading-point name.
Choose a topic (.irdeck).
Pick the first reading day (manual or recommended).
Optionally create a reading note or append a source marker, then confirm to enqueue and schedule.
Web: https://…
Vault links / block refs: [[Note]], [[Note#^blockId]]
PDF++ selection or bookmark links (including links inside PDF callouts)
Canvas nodes: [[board.canvas#^nodeId]]
EPUB location links (requires Weave EPUB Reader)

buttons.label: Markdown selection
buttons.description: Command “Create incremental reading point from selection”

buttons.label: Obsidian browser
buttons.description: Web viewer menu / selection → Add to incremental reading

buttons.label: Canvas node
buttons.description: Node menu → Add to incremental reading

import.title: When to import materials
paragraphs: Use Import reading materials when you want a whole Markdown file, PDF outline, or EPUB outline to become many reading points.
Entry: calendar “More” → Import reading materials.

items: Choose files (one batch = one type only: md / pdf / epub).
PDF / EPUB first show an outline step so you can pick chapters.
Choose a split mode and configure options.
Preview generated reading points, then confirm.

listGroups.heading: Markdown
items: Split by headings, blank lines, and similar rules; whole-file mode can reference or copy.
Compatibility import folder defaults to “plugin data folder / IR”.

listGroups.heading: PDF / EPUB (premium)
items: Create bookmark-style reading points from outlines with resume info.
EPUB outline parsing depends on Weave EPUB Reader.

import.title: Folder subscription
paragraphs: Folder subscription fits inbox / clipping workflows: choose a Markdown folder in your vault, and the plugin scans and auto-adds matching new materials into a bound topic, then schedules them into the incremental reading queue.
This differs from one-shot Import reading materials: import is a manual file-split action; subscription keeps watching a folder and topping up automatically.

items: Configure: Settings → Weave Incremental Reading → Basic → Subscribe clipping folders (add rules, choose folders, bind topics, initial schedule mode, bulk confirm threshold).
Manual sync: calendar More → Update subscribed folders, or the command “Update subscribed folders”.
Background sync also runs on plugin startup and relevant vault file changes.
Folder subscription is premium: without activation the entry may be hidden, or shown locked if “Show advanced feature preview” is on.

trace.title: Tracing principle
paragraphs: Each reading point stores a stable resume link and source kind. Opening from the calendar routes by type and locates the original position when possible.

trace.title: Canvas nodes
paragraphs: Add: Canvas node menu, or paste [[board.canvas#^nodeId]].
Resume: open the Canvas and highlight the node by ID (with text candidates if needed).
Requires: built-in Obsidian Canvas.

trace.title: Obsidian browser (web)
paragraphs: Add: Web Viewer “Add to incremental reading”, or paste an https URL; web points usually create a reading note.
Resume: open the URL in Obsidian’s browser.
Requires: Obsidian’s built-in web viewer.

trace.title: Weave EPUB Reader selection
paragraphs: Add: use “Add to incremental reading” from a reader selection, or paste an EPUB location link. Highlights alone do not become reading points.
Resume: open via the obsidian://weave-epub-reader protocol and locate by CFI / chapter.
Requires: Weave EPUB Reader.

trace.title: Obsidian Markdown
paragraphs: Add: block refs [[Note#^blockId]], line anchors, “Current location”, or selection quick-create.
Resume: open the note and scroll to the block or line, with a locate highlight when available.
Requires: native Obsidian Markdown.

trace.title: PDF (PDF++)
paragraphs: Add: paste PDF++ selection / bookmark links, or import chapters from an outline.
Resume: open the PDF and resolve page / selection anchors.
Requires: Obsidian PDF support; precise selections work best with PDF++.

items: Vault data: the source of truth for topics and reading points (back up and sync this).
Plugin folder: settings, cache, and runtime state (mostly rebuildable; prefer vault backups).

data.title: Vault data root
paragraphs: The default folder name is “weave Incremental reading” (configurable in settings). points, materials, registry, and related files live directly under it, isolated from the shared weave/ root used by other Weave plugins.
data.code:
weave Incremental reading/
  points/                 # .irdeck topic files
  materials/
  registry/
  pdf-bookmark-tasks.json
  epub-bookmark-tasks.json
  IR/                     # compatibility import folder

data.title: .irdeck topic files
paragraphs: Each topic is one .irdeck file: topic metadata plus a points array (schedule, trace, relations, and more). Cross-plugin workflows should treat .irdeck records as the L0 source of truth.

items: Settings live in .obsidian/plugins/weave-incremental-reading/data.json.
cache/ and state/ speed up local use; they need not match perfectly across machines.
Back up the whole plugin data folder (including every .irdeck). Confirm the old folder is ready before changing the data root.

family.title: What Weave is
paragraphs: Weave is a set of Obsidian plugins organized around read → capture → schedule → review.

Weave EPUB Reader handles in-vault reading and excerpts; the Weave main plugin handles decks, quizzes, and card creation; Weave Incremental Reading (this plugin) handles the reading queue and calendar.

listGroups.heading: Division of labor
items: Weave EPUB Reader: read books in Obsidian, manage highlights/excerpts, and link with notes, Canvas, and decks.
Weave main plugin: turn any source excerpt into traced memory cards, manage them in multiple views, and review with FSRS.
Weave Incremental Reading: turn “read later” into a reading-point queue scheduled by topics and a month calendar.

family.title: Weave Incremental Reading (this plugin)
paragraphs: Built for “collected too much, opened too many books, finished too little”: advance reading points on a calendar instead of relying on willpower alone.

listGroups.heading: Core features
items: Reading points and topics (.irdeck)
Incremental reading calendar, continuous reading, and load scheduling
Unified add-link flow, material import, and folder subscription
Associated notes (PDF / EPUB curated; Markdown / web outlinks) and tag groups (still being improved)
Source resume for Markdown / PDF / Canvas / web / EPUB

family.title: Weave main plugin
paragraphs: An Obsidian knowledge-card system: create traced memory cards from any vault excerpt, browse them in table/kanban/grid views, and practice with quizzes.

listGroups.heading: Core features
items: Excerpt-to-card creation and multi-view management
Quiz banks, wrong-answer sets, and exam stats
FSRS spaced repetition and study sessions
Optional license inheritance with this plugin

family.title: Weave EPUB Reader
paragraphs: Open EPUB and related formats inside your vault, excerpt while reading, and deep-link book locations to notes and incremental reading points.

listGroups.heading: With this plugin
items: Import EPUB chapters as reading points
Create located reading points from reader selections
Resume from the calendar into the reader at the original spot
Queue only: install this plugin alone.
Also read/resume EPUB chapters: this plugin + Weave EPUB Reader.
Also create cards and review: this plugin + Weave main plugin.
Full loop (read → capture → schedule → review): install all three.
